column3: Thomson problem: points on the unit sphere, Coulomb objective +inf wherever two coincide. The objective-encoding defects (#100) are fixed and are no longer the blocker. #110 tracked what remains until it was closed as not planned (2026-09-07); its elec criterion had been retired to #116 and #117, both closed, so no open issue tracks this failure. What remains is the Float jump: the .nl gives no finite variable bounds, so the box is the +/-1e9 inf-clamp, random init starts ~1e9 out, and driving each variable to 0 is a huge row improvement - which lands the search on the origin, a stationary point of every row x^2+y^2+z^2=1. The Float jump offers one undamped Newton step (x0 - residual/grad) plus lb/ub/midpoint; near the origin that step overshoots wildly and is rejected, and because a candidate was still generated the #107 escape probe is suppressed, so the variable freezes at score 0. Measured: the escape probe fires only at exactly x0=0; at x0=0.001/0.01/0.1 the score is 0 whether it is armed or not. Infeasible at violation ~1 with the objective present AND with it neutralised, so this is not objective-related. Tightening the inf-clamp to 1 makes elec25 feasible at violation 0 post-#100 (pre-#100 it was infeasible at every clamp), because clamping accidentally supplies the missing damping.
